reason: A logical flaw in the protocol's definition, found before any Reliance ranking, model or summary run: the baseline "O1" equals O1+S1 by definition, because S1 takes the first k of the ordering, so the ranking conditions pass on any data. The amendment responds to that flaw, not to any Reliance result.

baseline.name: retrieval_order
baseline.definition: search A's articles in the order returned, then search B's in the order returned; each article once; the frozen Stage 1 rules (cleaning and duplicates) applied with no other sorting; the surviving articles keep their relative order; the first k
baseline.note: the retrieval order of two searches, not NewsAPI's relevance ranking of one search

independence: not blind in the strictest sense: the labels and events exist when the amendment is made; it is written without reading them, and before any ranking result exists
absolute_values: precision, event recall and direct-event recall of both lists at every k, without a level
